title: I just noticed Google has deleted YEARS worth of photos from my backup
raw_text:
Hi, I have no idea where to start. I went to look up photos of my grandma, and I noticed most are now missing with no clue on when or how they ever got deleted. Ive been using Google photos since 2012 and many of my photos from 2012 up to 2019 are just GONE. Why and how did this happen?? Has this happened to anyone else and is there any way to get them back? 
 
Slight update: I still haven’t gotten many of my photos back BUT there are two things that helped a little: firstly searching for a month and year instead of scrolling through. The other may be to change your membership, I recently got the offer for a year free for the student member ship (the one that is 1TB, the pro version of Gemini, etc.) and I got some videos and photos back. It’s definitely not everything but it’s at least some. The support team has not been helpful but still trying to work toward a solution. 
 
Biggest thing, there are a lot of us who have had this experience!
author: rachelschmitz_

analysis.relevance_reasoning: The post concerns large-scale deletion of photos rather than a vague-memory retrieval problem; the user knows what they are looking for but the items are missing.
analysis.failure_evidence: most are now missing with no clue on when or how they ever got deleted
analysis.desired_outcome: recover the missing photos of grandma from the Google Photos backup

title: Google photos, what people don't understand in my opinion
raw_text: Google photos is so much more than a storage location. The ability to search for people, places, And other things that you haven't actually identified but Google AI does makes it so valuable. Recently I wanted to find a picture of myself and my wife sitting in front of some tulips about 5 years ago. So I just typed that description in and found it in 2 minutes. That's the kind of thing you can do in Google photos that you can't do in a standard storage environment.
author: twestheimer

analysis.relevance_reasoning: The post describes a successful search without any breakdown, friction, or workaround, so it does not pertain to vague‑memory retrieval failures.
analysis.desired_outcome: locate a specific personal photo of the user and spouse sitting in front of tulips from roughly five years ago
